source.title: List of unsolved problems in mathematics

accepted.question_text: Does the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture remain unsolved?
Does the Hodge conjecture remain unsolved?
Does the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem remain unsolved?
Does the P versus NP problem remain unsolved?
Does the Riemann hypothesis remain unsolved?
Does the Yang–Mills existence and mass gap problem remain unsolved?
Is the smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture true; that is, can a four-dimensional topological sphere carry two or more inequivalent smooth structures?

evidence.page: Millennium Prize Problems paragraph after item 6
evidence.quote: However, a generalization called the smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture—that is, whether a four-dimensional topological sphere can have two or more inequivalent smooth structures—is unsolved.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The page is a dynamic aggregate index containing hundreds of very short bullet-point problem names across many mathematical subfields, and many entries are not self-contained enough to be rewritten faithfully without processing the source in smaller section-level shards.

evidence.quote: This is a dynamic list and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness.

This list is a composite of notable unsolved problems mentioned in previously published lists, including but not limited to lists considered authoritative, and the problems listed here vary widely in both difficulty and importance.
